correctness.rationale: Each full inverse branch has Jacobian modulus 1/2; their exact average yields an invariant finite-dimensional affine transfer matrix. Its resolvent cofactor and determinant are computed symbolically for every M, with independent finite exact-rational identities for \(2\le M\le10\). The shortest offdiagonal return walk has length M and weight \(-2^{-(M+1)}\), proving the first negative lag. Jensen contraction plus inverse-branch equality excludes every unimodular centered-affine eigenfunction and justifies summing correlations. The bounded decomposition d=f+H-H∘F has \(Pd=0\), \(Pd^2=(1-y_1)^2/4\), and a uniform \([-1,1]\) variable \(d\), so the ergodic reverse martingale CLT gives variance 1/3. The finite checker is corroboration, not proof of unbounded dimensions.

originality.rationale: The original full text proves invariant Lebesgue measure, Bernoulli dynamics and periodic-spectrum equidistribution but does not give correlations of Euclidean coordinate observables. The most relevant published same-map record concerns eigenvalues of periodic-point derivative cocycles, not the volume transfer of affine observables. The accessible historical ledger contains same-map periodic orbit/multiplier claims but no matching coordinate autocovariance, first negative lag or dimension-free diffusion law. Classical martingale CLTs alone do not give the map-specific explicit coboundary or exact rational correlation function. Search absence is not uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: Search and indexed material cannot exclude an unpublished or unindexed coordinate-correlation derivation.

General methods for transfer of affine maps may make the calculation straightforward once formulated; originality rests on the new specific statistic, dimension-lag threshold and zero aggregate covariance, not on the transfer machinery.
Other published baker-map models are not claimed to share the same formula.

value.rationale: The first-coordinate signal is a canonical Euclidean observable in the twisted baker model of vortex dynamics. Its covariance has an exact dimension-\(M\) delay before the first negative value, even though known Bernoulli mixing by itself supplies no such geometric-time scale. A full rational transform determines all lags, and an explicit reverse-martingale decomposition produces the surprising dimension-free long-time variance despite changing short-time correlations. This is a substantive natural dynamical observable, not a renamed general theorem or isolated numerical special case.
